mine_p05_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_001.text: On Day 470, Lei An took Lin to the wildlife notice beside the surface garden. The observer's name was Jia Wen. She asked for sightings from cleared places, including weather, time and ordinary disturbance, and specifically asked people not to collect the grey moths. Lei pointed out a ragged patch of writing where rain had loosened the paper. Jia arrived carrying a replacement sheet and a basket of observation markers. Her first field task was to keep the request readable, not reveal what the mountain wanted.

mine_p05_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_002.text: Jia had worked around Vermilion Hollows for several seasons. She was employed for the stated habitat observations, with safety decisions about mine structure left to Fan and the ordinary work leads. Lin asked whether the moths caused the ticking people called the living seam. Jia said she had evidence of larvae in some exposed mineral cracks and did not yet know which sounds came from which sources. She could show Lin a permitted observation place. She would not turn a local association into a conclusion about every noise below.

mine_p05_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_003.text: They walked to a warm wall outside the receiving gallery. Its stones had been stacked years earlier, and a narrow mineral face remained exposed behind an ordinary drain. Lin could approach only from the cleared path. Jia showed the standing markers and asked her to watch one short interval before speaking. A grey moth rested against the red stain. Its wings moved once without leaving the stone. The little movement made Lin more attentive than a grand description of a spirit beast would have done.

mine_p05_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_004.text: A second moth crossed the wall and settled above the first. Neither offered a message. Jia described the visible features which distinguished this observed colony from a household moth near stored grain. The grey seam moths used a mineral-associated habitat, and their species-specific cultivation rhythm was not a human stage chart. An external response could indicate compatible conditions for them without measuring a cultivator's reserve. Lin watched the resting insects and realized how much human ambition could fit inside the word compatible.

mine_p05_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_005.text: Jia kept a comparison marker away from the insects rather than directing it at a wing. The prepared observation apparatus had its own rating and energy source. Lin supplied no qi. The marker's response belonged to an external field comparison under the observer's method. It did not tell them what an insect remembered, how much a person could retain, or whether a roof was sound. Jia entered the actual setup and interval while Lin drew the positions she could see from the standing place.

mine_p05_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_006.text: The warmer part of the wall held more resting moths than the shaded corner during that interval. Lin suggested warmth might explain the difference. Jia wrote it as a question and showed the previous day's ordinary temperature notes. Wind and surface moisture had also changed. The next observation would compare the relevant conditions without forcing the insects into a box to obtain a cleaner result. Lin liked having a possible explanation and found it harder to leave it possible than she had expected.

mine_p05_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_007.text: A mine worker named Luo Ping approached with an empty lunch basket. He said the moths had appeared after Lu Sen died and asked whether they carried the worker's spirit. Jia asked which year he remembered seeing them first. Luo considered the question and admitted he had seen them as a child, long before the accident. The association belonged to later stories. Lin did not laugh. Memory could move two events closer together when one had acquired a grief the other seemed able to hold.

mine_p05_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_008.text: Luo said his aunt still called them little singers. The observer accepted the family name as a name and kept it separate from her field finding. He watched one moth lift from the warm stone, circle the drain and settle again. He asked whether it could hear him. Jia said there were observations of response to certain disturbances, and today's interval did not establish response to his words. Luo lowered his voice anyway. Lin thought a person could choose courtesy without being told that the creature understood the reason.

mine_p05_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_009.text: A small tapping reached them from the exposed crack. Jia marked its time and the surface conditions. She did not open the crack or ask Lin to follow it with a new internal technique. The site was being observed through an agreed standing place. A maintenance worker checked the ordinary drain from the cleared side and reported water moving as expected. Two things happened close together: a field sound and an ordinary service check. Their proximity did not make the drain worker a beast expert or the observer a drain inspector.

mine_p05_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_010.text: Lin's drawing was poor. She made the wall too straight and the two moths too alike. Jia asked which details would let another observer find the same positions. They added the drain edge, the marker and the visible stain. Artistic confidence mattered less than a usable reference. Lin remembered the highest-quality portraits she had seen in wealthy rooms and felt embarrassed by her scratchy insects. Jia showed her an old field drawing with an equally ugly arrow and a useful date. The observation did not require beauty to become checkable.

mine_p05_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_011.text: The agreed interval ended before Lin began to feel she understood the wall. Jia closed the marker record and left the colony undisturbed. A remaining question was a reason to schedule another observation, not stay until fatigue made every moth movement look significant. Lin walked back to the garden with the sounds still in her attention. She had spent time with living creatures whose response was local and unfamiliar. Nothing in the experience had advanced her human routes.

mine_p05_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_012.text: That afternoon Lin completed an ordinary walk around the permitted surface garden before supper. She saw moths near a stone warmed by the kitchen's outer flue and none on the wet fence during that short visit. She had not held the conditions constant. The note would remain a casual sighting which might guide a later check. Lei asked if she had found the mountain's secret. Lin showed the badly drawn wall instead. Lei said the insects looked like burnt buns, which was a fairer criticism than prophecy.

mine_p05_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_013.text: Jia scheduled a second short observation for Day 472. Lin checked that it fell outside her accepted mine half-day and agreed to attend as a permitted observer. The role did not become unpaid permanent monitoring. Jia had staff time and equipment budget for her actual survey, while Lin's contribution stayed bounded. The ordinary work arrangement gave her a livelihood; the field interval offered learning. She wanted both, and neither would remain honest if she let one quietly swallow the time promised to the other.

mine_tool_followup.speaker: narrator
mine_tool_followup.text: On Day 471, the hammer dispute returned to her attention through the people affected by it. Zeng Bo's tool had been released under the corrected owner comparison. His delay claim and the mine's response arrangements had followed the actual help he accepted. Lin would not pretend that every possible route through the dispute had occurred. She went to the surface lane after her own work, ready to meet the consequence her commitment had left there. The moths could wait while another living matter required a person's answer.

mine_p05_public_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_public_001.text: The public correction contact was holding its first scheduled interval. Ren Tao sat at the allocated desk with an assistant covering the normal receiving board. A worker brought a privately owned lamp-glass frame held under a combined bundle mismatch. The contact acknowledged the request, identified the needed source holder and gave a response date. Lin watched from the public waiting place. The service Zeng's account had helped create was doing work through its actual assigned staff, rather than through the hope that she might happen to pass.

mine_p05_public_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_public_002.text: The lamp worker did not consent to a wider interview about her household expenses. Ren recorded the correction question and left those expenses out. She said she wanted her frame returned, not another audience. Lin recognized that wish from Zeng's different public choice. A new service could be available without making every user a public example. The worker took the acknowledged reference and went back to her own shift. Its usefulness would be measured by the answer she actually received.

mine_p05_public_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_public_003.text: Zeng came with the full tool roll and sat beside Lin briefly. He had read the notice and wanted to see whether its first interval existed outside the printed sheet. Ren greeted him without asking him to remain as a permanent witness. Zeng looked relieved at that small freedom. The public case had altered the mine's process, and his own role could end. He told Lin the hammer's new handle felt strange but sound, then asked whether the grey moths really sang.

mine_p05_public_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_public_004.text: Lin described the observed tapping and Jia's uncertainty about its sources. Zeng said he would ask the observer about sightings near his ordinary surface workshop. His question did not include entering a closed heading or lending his hammer as a specimen tool. He might report a permitted sighting from a place he already used. The public correction meeting had given him confidence that a small observation could reach a responsible person. That was a changed relationship with the mine, not an extra qi capacity.

mine_p05_public_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_public_005.text: The contact's first answer reached the lamp worker two days later through the accepted source comparison. Its owner field was corrected and the frame released. Lin heard the permitted public disposition from Ren while performing her normal board task. She did not add the worker's private life to her account. The twice-weekly trial service had completed one specific matter. It would still need staffing and review over the six agreed weeks, including the requests which might prove harder than the first one.

mine_p05_private_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_private_001.text: Zeng invited Lin to his surface workshop after her mine half-day. No public correction service had been created from his confidential claim. Sui's internal referral note had changed, and the particular hammer entry was corrected. Zeng liked that the shop visitors did not know his private job terms. He showed Lin a small stool leg he was repairing for an ordinary customer. The work had a separate accepted price and would be tested for its intended load before return.

mine_p05_private_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_private_002.text: The hammer's new handle lay comfortably in his hand now. He used it for a light fitting task and stopped before discussing his father again. This time he did not need to explain why the head mattered. Lin had heard that part privately. She asked about the ordinary joint instead, and he showed which gap had caused the stool to rock. Their shared conversation could move away from grievance without declaring the grievance unimportant. He finished the permitted work while she stood clear of the tool.

mine_p05_private_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_private_003.text: A grey moth settled on the workshop's warm outer wall. Zeng called it a little singer, the same name Luo Ping's aunt used. Lin told him about Jia's permitted sighting request. He agreed to submit the location and time, without offering his family recollections as evidence of the creature's meaning. Lin drew the wall edge from the ordinary lane with his permission. The note contained a living insect and an observed place. It would not expose the confidential account which had brought her to the workshop.

mine_p05_private_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_private_004.text: At supper, Tao Mei asked whether Lin had learned a method for making moths carry messages. Lin said she had learned how easily she wanted an answer after watching a short interval. Tao found that more convincing than a new technique. Lan said she wanted a moth to deliver complaints about cabbage. Her mother said the moth would need permission from the kitchen first. They laughed at the imagined bureaucracy without making a field claim from the joke. Lin stayed until the lamps were lit and then left for her own rest.

mine_p05_private_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_private_005.text: The confidential route had preserved Zeng's chosen privacy and made room for ordinary friendship around his work. Other workers still had to find the existing source contacts when their own tools were held. Lin kept that public limit in view when she returned to the mine office. She could support a separately consented request for change later. She could not use the family's supper or the quiet workshop visit as permission to publish the claim they had chosen to keep bounded.

mine_p05_pause_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_pause_001.text: Zeng passed Lin in the surface lane carrying his repaired hammer and a newly accepted crate-handle task. He greeted her without stopping long. Luo Bin had helped him obtain the corrected release after the later appointment. The supported delay question remained with its proper reviewer. Lin asked only whether the new ordinary work was going well. He said the customer had waited and then moved on toward the workshop. The brief exchange was friendly enough to continue and did not erase the earlier distance.

mine_p05_pause_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_pause_002.text: Lin went to the observation garden by herself. The time she had kept from representation remained available for her own bounded learning and rest. It was not a repayment to Zeng. She had no authority to count his eventual private fee as a benefit she had delivered. In her notes, Luo's actual source work stayed beside the corrected return. The relationship which followed her choice was quieter than the friendship that might have grown from sharing a claim meeting, and she let it be quieter.

mine_p05_pause_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_pause_003.text: Near the warm wall, she saw a grey moth on an ordinary discarded packing strip. The strip lay outside the colony standing markers and belonged to the site's waste sorting. Lin told the maintenance attendant rather than picking it up as a specimen. Jia later came to observe the resting insect under her own permitted work. Lin had supplied a location from an accessible path. She did not need Zeng's workshop invitation or a publicly reformed desk to make that particular ordinary report.

mine_p05_pause_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_pause_004.text: Luo Bin arrived at the public notice shelter with a different worker's source request. He asked Lin where Ren's ordinary receiving interval stood. She pointed to the posted hours and did not assume he was acting for Zeng again. The helper's work continued through people who were not part of her earlier decision. Lin watched him write down the time. Declining a role had left space for someone else's actual contribution, and that person had more than one story to work on.

mine_p05_pause_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_pause_005.text: Later Zeng paused at Han's doorway long enough to tell Lin the crate customer had paid the agreed fee after accepting the repaired handle. He did not ask her to attend his family supper. She congratulated him on finished work and returned to her own table. The greeting carried less intimacy than a shared private comparison would have carried, without becoming hostility. Her choice had preserved personal time and limited the relationship. Those were ordinary consequences she could live with instead of forcing every encounter to provide reassurance.

mine_p05_after_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_001.text: On Day 472, Jia and Lin returned to the warm wall under the same permitted standing arrangement. The sky was overcast, the exposed surface cooler, and fewer adult moths rested there during the interval. The observer retained wind and moisture notes instead of declaring temperature the only cause. Lin found the smaller count unexpectedly disappointing. She had wanted the first question to reward attention with an answer. The colony had no obligation to arrange itself into a lesson at the speed of her curiosity.

mine_p05_after_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_002.text: They heard tapping again after a fine drizzle began. Jia marked the interval and compared it with the earlier sound record. A larval movement might contribute in the exposed crack; water could also move loose mineral grains; the gallery's distant work had its own sounds. Lin listened to three possible sources without merging them. The living seam name could remain useful local speech while the actual field account stayed unresolved in particular places. Uncertainty did not mean nothing had been learned.

mine_p05_after_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_003.text: A worker carrying an ordinary stone sample asked whether they wanted it placed near the colony. Jia declined because an unregistered change would alter the observation. The sample had its own accepted destination in the materials room. Lin stepped aside while he carried it there. He said people below had once fed the moths crumbs, thinking it kind. Jia described the diet questions and asked that nobody introduce food during the survey. A creature's unfamiliar needs did not become simpler because a human gift was affectionate.

mine_p05_after_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_004.text: They visited the permitted edge of an older spoil heap on Day 475 after Lin's mine half-day. An ordinary site attendant escorted them along the inspected path. Small grey wings appeared near mineral flakes exposed by recent rain. The habitat observations now concerned two permitted surface places. Jia did not use them as proof that the colony filled an inaccessible seam. Lin drew the slope badly and marked the standing position clearly. The point was where another observer could repeat the sighting, not how far she could make the mountain seem alive.

mine_p05_after_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_005.text: The spoil heap held remnants of older work. Some stone had been rejected for extraction, some mixed material needed ordinary handling under the site's rules, and coarse plants covered settled areas. Jia asked the attendant which portions had been disturbed recently. The answer came from actual maintenance records, not the color of the dust alone. Lin saw a moth lift from a newly exposed edge and wondered whether the disturbance had displaced it. The question would need other observations before anyone blamed the miners or dismissed the effect.

mine_p05_after_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_006.text: Fan Luwei met them at the path junction. He said a planned drain repair could change the accessible observation place and asked Jia to coordinate its interval with the habitat survey. The ordinary drainage work had a safety purpose and could not wait indefinitely for perfect field conditions. Jia described what could be observed before and after the change without obstructing the crew. Lin watched two qualified roles negotiate a useful comparison instead of competing to make their subject the only thing which mattered.

mine_p05_after_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_007.text: The drain crew repaired the ordinary surface channel on Day 477. Jia observed from the agreed safe standing place and retained the changed-condition record. Lin was at her accepted mine work during part of the repair and attended only afterward. Her notes identified which events she had seen and which came from the responsible crew's report. A drawing could contain a later repaired channel without implying she had watched every tool stroke that produced it.

mine_p05_after_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_008.text: Afterward the exposed corner stayed less wet during a short interval with similar light rain. Fewer adult moths rested at that particular corner while other parts of the wall still held sightings. Jia did not call it a successful eviction or a complete habitat loss. She compared the limited observations and planned the next check. Lin found the change sadder than she expected. An ordinary repair could protect workers and affect living creatures at the same time. A useful safety purpose did not make the second consequence imaginary.

mine_p05_after_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_009.text: Lei An asked whether the colony should be moved somewhere safer. Jia explained that moving unfamiliar larvae could damage them and that she had not established a suitable alternative habitat. A protective decision would need actual evidence, scope and responsible people. For now the survey recommended avoiding unnecessary disturbance outside the accepted repair and retaining the observation marks. Lin saw how a modest recommendation could be more protective than an ambitious promise to rescue everything she had learned to care about during a week.

mine_p05_after_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_010.text: Luo Ping brought his aunt to the public sighting shelter on Day 479. She introduced herself as Shen Tao and asked whether the little singers still gathered near the old warm wall. Jia showed the permitted observations without identifying private workers' sources. Shen remembered feeding crumbs as a child and accepted that the practice should stop during the survey. She did not treat correction as an insult to her family memory. She asked how to tell the grey moth from the household kind, and Jia showed the visible distinctions within the limits of her field knowledge.

mine_p05_after_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_011.text: Shen spoke of Lu Sen's song only after the moth discussion. The recording's holder had heard the same ticking in its background and some people now claimed it answered them. She had known Lu when he was alive and missed his habit of singing the final line twice when tired. Lin listened to a memory which belonged to a living witness. Shen did not ask her to bring him back. She wanted the family-authorized song treated as more than a curious noise visitors could play until it lost its privacy.

mine_p05_after_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_012.text: Lin asked where the source's current permission could be read. Shen named the responsible custodian and said the family had limited playback appointments. Her answer created a possible inquiry route, not access already granted. Jia kept the record question separate from the insect observations. A sound copied during older work might help identify conditions in one scene, but it could not turn the moths into Lu's continuing mind. Lin felt the difference become personal when Shen said she still remembered the living man's face better than the recording remembered anything.

mine_p05_after_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_013.text: On Day 481, Jia completed the first survey summary from the permitted surface intervals. It named locations, changed conditions, limited sightings and unresolved sound sources. She thanked Lin for the bounded assistance and retained responsibility for the actual report. Lin had her own permitted drawing and a clearer set of questions. She returned to the receiving yard without a captured moth or a new cultivation technique. The mountain contained life worth studying, and people whose work and memories would have to remain distinct within that study.

mine_p05_after_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_014.text: A herb seller came to the public sighting shelter while Jia was replacing a weather sheet. He called himself Peng Yun and carried a jar containing grey wings. Lin first thought the contents were moths. Jia looked through the glass and identified cast wings mixed with unrelated fragments, without opening the jar at the field station. Peng said a buyer had supplied them as seam-moth material. He had hoped the observer would certify the lot before he offered it to cultivators.

mine_p05_after_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_015.text: Jia refused the proposed certification because she had not established the material's source, identity or appropriate use. Peng became defensive. He had paid for it, and the buyer would not take it back without a finding. Ownership did not answer the biological questions. Lin watched him turn the jar as if the fragments might arrange themselves into proof. The seller was neither a great villain nor a reliable witness merely because his own money had been spent. He was a worried person standing between a supplier's claim and a customer's possible harm.

mine_p05_after_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_016.text: He asked Lin whether her six paired routes could identify the fragments. She said her human practice did not qualify her for that task. Peng's face closed. He had expected a cultivator to want a remedy which sounded rare. Lin did want progress, and the jar made that wanting uncomfortably visible. She could imagine paying for a compatible substance and discovering the promise had moved faster than its evidence. Jia directed the seller to the actual material-assessment service and kept the habitat survey separate from his commercial dispute.

mine_p05_after_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_017.text: The assessment appointment would cost time and the stated ordinary fee. Peng said a richer seller could carry the jar across town without noticing either cost. Jia agreed that resources affected access and did not offer to erase the standard. She gave him the public service hours and the route for asking about the accepted fee terms. Lin did not buy the fragments to relieve his embarrassment. Her sympathy would otherwise become an unexamined remedy in her own pack and leave the original question unanswered.

mine_p05_after_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_018.text: After Peng left, Lin admitted that she had been tempted to ask whether the colony's compatible field could help her bridge preparation. Jia said the temptation was a useful question if it stayed a question. The insects used their own physiology and environment. An external association did not prescribe a human input. Lin felt disappointed without feeling corrected out of existence. She would eventually need an independent human curriculum, not a field observation made more exciting by her desire to use it.

mine_p05_after_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_019.text: On the next visit, a child named Ru Ru stood at the sighting rope holding a small paper box. Her father explained that a household moth had fallen into washing water and she wanted somebody to make it fly again. Jia checked the ordinary insect from outside the colony work. One wing was badly damaged. She could help keep it out of the water and describe its present condition. She did not promise that a grown wing would become whole because the child cried hard enough.

mine_p05_after_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_020.text: Ru asked Lin if qi could do the part Jia could not. Lin knelt beside the box and said she had no healing technique for the insect. The child pushed it toward her anyway. For a moment Lin hated the limits which made her answer small. She put a clean dry scrap where Jia directed and watched the moth find a steadier position. The act was useful and did not restore the wing. Ru's father stayed beside his daughter rather than asking the visitor to stop the tears with a spectacle.

mine_p05_after_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_021.text: They left the household moth in an appropriate sheltered ordinary place under Jia's limited guidance, away from the observed seam colony. Ru named the damaged wing Crooked and asked if it would remember her. Her father said they would remember trying to help it. Lin walked back to the standing marker with a heaviness she had not expected from a tiny creature. Attention could create responsibility without creating the power to produce the ending somebody wanted.

mine_p05_after_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_022.text: Jia was quiet during the next field interval. Lin asked whether such requests happened often. The observer said people generally reached the person whose work looked nearest to their problem. Sometimes that person could help, sometimes could only direct them, and sometimes had to say a clear no. The difficulty was making the boundary useful rather than turning it into a wall nobody could understand. Lin thought of Zeng's hammer, Peng's jar and Ru's box. Three requests had required different answers from the same surface shelter.

mine_p05_after_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_023.text: Qiao later read the first habitat summary with Jia at the public planning table. A marked undisturbed edge beside the spoil heap could remain outside ordinary storage without blocking the necessary drain repair. A more controlled surface comparison could refine the water-and-warmth observations. Both required actual allocated time. Jia could continue her basic survey without Lin accepting another role. The forewoman asked which proposed work would use the available interval, not whether everyone loved living creatures enough to promise every possible protective action.

mine_p05_after_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_024.text: Peng Yun returned without the jar two days later. He had decided not to sell the unidentified fragments while seeking the supplier response. That choice tied up money he wanted for stock. Lin asked whether he had obtained a reply. He said not yet, then bought warm soup instead of asking her to certify anything. His problem remained difficult without making the difficulty somebody else's untested medicine.

mine_p05_after_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_025.text: Ru Ru later showed Lin the empty paper box. The household moth had died. Her father had helped her bury it beside a garden stone. Lin listened while Ru explained where the stone stood and then asked if grey moths could still visit. She said living moths might come for their reasons. The child's burial could preserve her care without promising that a visitor would be the creature she missed.

mine_habitat_choice.speaker: narrator
mine_habitat_choice.text: Lin could accept a bounded turn helping establish the marked buffer, join Jia's permitted changed-condition comparison, or decline ongoing habitat work and leave her drawing as an offered source. Each choice would leave a different practical contribution for the coming tailings discussion. None authorized collecting moths, opening a closed seam or using an insect's external rhythm as human cultivation instruction. Jia named the offered time and ordinary payment. Lin considered the work alongside her mine half-days and the rest she would need before seeking a new curriculum.

choices.text: Help establish the staffed, marked surface buffer.
Assist Jia's bounded changed-condition field comparison.
Offer your drawing and decline ongoing habitat work.

mine_p05_after_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_after_027.text: That evening Lei put an ordinary lamp near the lodging window while Lin repaired a loose tie on her pack. A household moth circled the light and struck the frame repeatedly. Lei opened the window enough for it to leave without disturbing the room's warmth too much. Neither companion called the small rescue a proof about the seam colony. Lin watched the creature vanish into the dark. Learning one unfamiliar habitat had made her more attentive to another ordinary life, without making every wing in the world part of the same mystery.

mine_habitat_buffer.speaker: narrator
mine_habitat_buffer.text: Lin accepted the marked-buffer turn. Jia and Qiao agreed the unused surface edge which could be left undisturbed while ordinary drain work continued. On Day 482, Lin worked one two-hour assistant interval at the cleared path, holding the public location sheet while the responsible site crew placed the markers. She did not certify slope stability. Fan accepted the ordinary standing arrangement separately. The result was a visible boundary which workers could use without needing Lin nearby to explain a private drawing.

mine_p05_buffer_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_buffer_002.text: A cart attendant objected that the new marker would lengthen one light empty-cart return. Qiao walked the alternative with him and entered the actual diversion in the issued task plan. The buffer was small enough to accept, not costless. Lin followed from the cleared path and saw why people who supported a colony could still dislike an extra walk. Jia recorded the accepted change. The marker's purpose would survive better if its practical inconvenience remained visible than if every complaint were treated as hostility to living things.

mine_p05_buffer_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_buffer_003.text: The observer paid Lin two coppers for the completed two-hour turn from the allocated assistant budget. Lin retained her wage receipt, while the marker sheets stayed with their responsible holders. The pay covered placement assistance, not a future duty to guard the colony at night. She asked the cart attendant how the diversion felt after his next ordinary turn. He said manageable with an empty cart and wanted the condition retained. Qiao would not expand it to a loaded route without another accepted check.

mine_p05_buffer_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_buffer_004.text: On Day 483, Jia compared sightings inside the marked edge with the earlier permitted intervals. Some moths rested there and others did not. The buffer had reduced unnecessary disturbance in one place; it had not commanded the colony to thrive or solved every tailings question. Lin watched a grey wing settle beneath the marker's ordinary wooden shadow. A small physical protection existed now because people had accepted and staffed it. Its later use would require keeping that boundary compatible with the actual work around it.

mine_p05_buffer_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_buffer_005.text: Lei An said the little public boundary would give visiting children a place to watch without pursuing insects behind carts. Jia added that use only within the already accepted standing condition. Lin liked the prospect of a child asking about visible wings before asking for prophecy. She had helped establish something other people could use. Her later cultivation examination would still depend on human practice, reserve, compatible input and recovered tissue. The moths had received a buffer rather than a place on her stage chart.

mine_habitat_comparison.speaker: narrator
mine_habitat_comparison.text: Lin accepted the changed-condition comparison turn. Jia scheduled one two-hour assistant interval on Day 482, outside her mine half-day, with two cleared surface references and the existing observation apparatus. Lin would record ordinary setup, moisture and sightings while Jia handled the prepared field comparison. No insects would be collected or relocated. Fan accepted the standing places separately. The purpose was to improve a limited habitat question, not test whether a human bridge could imitate the rhythm of a mineral-associated colony.

mine_p05_comparison_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_comparison_002.text: The first placement gave an unstable ordinary reference because water rocked the supporting stone. Lin caught the movement before Jia entered a field result. They moved to the accepted stable reference and retained the failed setup note. The second placement was suitable. A less flattering record made their actual comparison more useful. Lin felt pleased for a moment, then checked that pleasure against the task. Catching an external setup problem did not qualify her to diagnose her own governing vessel from a similar sensation.

mine_p05_comparison_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_comparison_003.text: Jia paid two coppers for Lin's completed two-hour assistant interval from the allocated observation budget. The data remained with the survey's responsible holder, and Lin retained only her permitted personal note and wage receipt. The result suggested moisture changes should be compared separately from warmth at those particular references. It did not prove how every accessible crack supported larvae. Jia would bring the limited finding into the later tailings discussion with its source places and changed conditions still attached.

mine_p05_comparison_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_comparison_004.text: On Day 483, the observer repeated a short interval without Lin's paid assistance and reported the permitted public disposition afterward. Lin had not observed that repeat herself. The repeated setup supported the earlier limited comparison but left several sound sources unresolved. She wrote the report as a report. The completed assistant turn had given Jia a better checked question and Lin experience resisting a false clear result. The comparison would need that patience, especially when an attractive answer arrived before the evidence did.

mine_p05_comparison_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_comparison_005.text: Lei An asked whether the comparison had saved the moths. Lin said it had improved what Jia could support about two surface conditions. Lei rolled his eyes at the careful answer and then asked which conditions. The conversation became more interesting once the result was small enough to explain. No new public buffer had been placed through Lin's choice. Existing protections and the necessary drain work continued under their own arrangements, while the later tailings discussion would receive a narrower piece of actual evidence.

mine_habitat_leave.speaker: narrator
mine_habitat_leave.text: Lin declined an ongoing habitat role and offered Jia the permitted drawing she had already made. The observer accepted it as a limited source and continued the basic survey through her allocated work. Lin received no assistant payment for a turn she had not performed. The marked standing places and the necessary ordinary drain work remained under their existing arrangements. She left the shelter with time for her own errands and a sense of unfinished responsibility which was not the same as an unaccepted contract.

mine_p05_leave_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_leave_002.text: On Day 482, she repaired a loosened pack tie and took an ordinary rest interval before her next mine half-day. The quiet felt less impressive than placing a buffer or improving a comparison. It was nevertheless the time she had chosen to preserve. Jia's field work continued without a new role for her. Lin would have the basic permitted survey summary at the later tailings discussion, not a personal assistant's record of an additional comparison. Declining needed an actual limit on what she could later claim.

mine_p05_leave_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_leave_003.text: Lei An asked if the moths had stopped interesting her. Lin said interest could remain while a person declined another task. Lei considered that answer and admitted he had stopped offering every evening to the lamp store after noticing how little time remained for his own meals. They sat beside the repaired window and discussed ordinary plans. The conversation did not make Jia's limited survey budget larger. It gave Lin companionship in a decision which left some useful work unchosen.

mine_p05_leave_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_leave_004.text: Jia greeted Lin in the yard on Day 483 and did not ask her to reconsider. She said the retained drawing had helped locate one earlier observation, then moved on to an accepted field appointment. The basic summary would keep its actual limits. No new public buffer or controlled comparison had been added through Lin's contribution. Lin appreciated the clear continuation. A declined role could remain declined without becoming a damaged relationship somebody had to mend by offering twice as much work later.

mine_p05_leave_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p05_leave_005.text: That evening Lin watched a grey moth from the ordinary lodging path and entered no formal sighting. Jia had the current survey, and casual observation did not have to become unpaid monitoring whenever Lin looked toward a wall. She enjoyed the wing's brief movement, then went inside for supper. The choice had preserved time and limited her later field evidence. It had not removed the colony, punished it for lacking human usefulness or turned her curiosity into a resource the mine could claim.
